chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān said: I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام,
Standing in the salat (prayer) has become very difficult for me.

He said: “When you want to attain the salat (prayer) of one who is standing, then recite while you are sitting. Then when two verses remain from the surah, stand up and complete what remains, and perform rukuʿ and sajdah. That is the salat (prayer) of one who is standing.”

key_terms.آيَتَانِ: two verses remaining from the surah
key_terms.السُّورَةِ: the surah being recited in the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الْقَائِمِ: the prayer reckoned as that of one standing

ai.seo_question: How should a person pray if standing during salat becomes difficult?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal concession for one who finds standing in salat (prayer) difficult. It explains that such a person may begin recitation while seated, then stand for the end of the recitation before rukuʿ and sajdah, and this is counted as the prayer of one standing.
